I changed SCIM user creation so it always creates users in local storage. I couldn't compile or test it: `mvn compile` on the `scim/model` module failed because the sibling Keycloak modules aren't installed.

In `UserResourceTypeProvider.onCreate`, I replaced `UserProfile.create(false)` with `UserStoragePrivateUtil.userLocalStorage(session).addUser(realm, username)`. The old call went through `session.users().addUser()`, which could pick a federation provider that has sync registration, such as LDAP in import mode. A user created that way came back from `POST /Users` with an ID but could not be fetched, because SCIM reads only look at local storage. The attribute population and `persist()` steps that follow are unchanged, so profile validation still applies. The default user-profile factory also just calls `addUser(realm, username)`, so the local call does the same creation work.

I did not add a SCIM federation strategy or any query of federation providers' capabilities, which the issue lists as optional.

The first graph queries were slow, and `find` was disabled, so I had to locate `UserResourceTypeProvider` through `impact UserStoragePrivateUtil.userLocalStorage`.
